alt: A single full-bleed strip, one finished wallpaper from each fractal family.
caption: One finished wallpaper per family, and nothing else about them is hand-made: each was found by a walk, drawn in one of the rendering modes, colored from a chosen palette, and kept by a judge.

alt: The four stages as a diagram: search feeds render, render feeds color, color feeds select.
caption: The pipeline end to end. Search proposes locations, render draws them at quality, color dresses them, and select keeps the few worth keeping — the four stages the rest of this site takes one at a time.

alt: Animated: three starting points advancing in step across the plane — one escaping fast, one bounded, one lingering near the boundary — with a |z|-versus-step chart alongside.
caption: Three orbits under the same rule, stepping together. One is past |z| = 2 within a few steps and gone for good, one stays bounded forever, and one hangs near the boundary for dozens of steps before it commits. The step where a track crosses the line on the chart is that orbit's escape time — the whole of what the picture is painted from.

alt: A strip of successive zooms into one point on the Mandelbrot boundary, each frame the marked box of the frame before it.
caption: One point on the boundary, magnified in stages, each frame drawn from the marked box of the one before. Nothing simplifies on the way down: spirals, filament tangles and miniature copies of the whole set keep arriving. The strip ends because the page does, not because the detail ran out.

alt: The Mandelbrot set as an atlas: several c values marked on it, each with the Julia set it produces beside it — a solid blob from deep inside, disconnected dust from outside, a filigree from the boundary.
caption: The Mandelbrot set read as an atlas of Julia sets. A c from deep inside gives a solid, rounded blob; a c from outside shatters into dust; a c from the boundary unfurls its neighborhood's spirals and filaments across the whole frame. The blob-versus-dust split is not a matter of degree — a Julia set is connected exactly when its c lies in the Mandelbrot set.

alt: The degree-3, degree-4 and degree-5 multibrot sets beside the classic degree-2 set, with one zoom each.
caption: Raising the power in z → z^d + c, with one zoom under each set. Every degree adds a rotational symmetry the classic set doesn't have — one fold fewer than the degree — and each carries its own Julia sets, made exactly the same way as before.

alt: Sets at fractional degrees d = 0.5, 1.5, 1.9, 2.1, 2.5 and 2.9, with a zoom or two showing the branch-cut seams.
caption: Between the whole numbers the shapes morph continuously, and the renders carry sharp seams where orbits cross the branch cut. The seam is a consequence of having to pick a branch of the complex logarithm rather than of the dynamics — a different branch is a different picture, which is why these are not one of the project's core families.

alt: The classic Ushiki phoenix render beside several finds from elsewhere in the (c, p) plane.
caption: The celebrated Ushiki constants beside finds from elsewhere in the (c, p) plane. Each orbit is steered by where it just was, and the feathery plumes are what that produces — structure none of the memoryless families draw.

alt: Six panels, one per family, each showing the whole set inside its own frame.
caption: Every family at its home view — the frame it draws when no viewport is given. Five of the six are derived by measuring the set and giving it a 16:9 frame with a tenth of the deciding axis to spare; a Julia set's extent depends on its constant, so it keeps the whole-plane view by exception.

alt: The same Mandelbrot view twice: smooth on the left, banded into flat contours on the right.
caption: One location, one palette, one iteration cap, two rendering modes. The discrete field is exactly the floor of the smooth one, so the difference is visible only where a frame holds few escape values — here, a cap of 50. At production caps the two are the same picture.

alt: A Phoenix set framed two ways: cropped at both lobes on the left, wholly contained on the right.
caption: Where a walk starts decides what it can find. On the left the root frame is the whole-plane default and holds 66% of the set's height; on the right it is the family's own home view, and both lobes are territory the walk can descend into.
